technical: The title says 'in Splunk' for the receive-telemetry result, but Splunk was only read back for the preview run with receive telemetry off. Fix: Either add a Splunk read-back of 10 sampled receive_preview traces to fix.sh and report the found and both-services counts, or retitle without 'in Splunk' for this result. For example: 'OTel Java Agent 3.0 Preview on SQS: Consumers Stay in the Producer's Trace, Even With Receive Telemetry On'.

technical: The title and opening say the receive spans stay in the one trace. The lab's own output shows the process span joining the producer's trace while the receive spans only link to it. With 72 receive spans for 100 messages, a receive span cannot be the child of each message's producer. Fix: Rewrite to: 'the process span stays in the producer's trace, and receive spans (now CLIENT kind) link to the producer traces'. Remove 'receive spans included' and 'Receive Spans ... Stay' from the title.

technical: The lab path in the post does not match the published lab, so the reproduce steps fail as written. Fix: Point the git clone, the cd path and the footer link at the real lab slug and repository, then run the three commands once from a clean checkout.

editorial: The post does not say that maintainers already describe this behaviour, so the headline result reads as new when it confirms the plan in issue 19414. Fix: Under 'What changed in the trace', add one sentence: the maintainers describe this in issue 19414, and this run confirms it on a real SQS queue and in Splunk APM. The operation-name table then becomes the post's own contribution.
outside claim without a known source: The Postgres preview article covers the database side

failures: title claim not found in evidence: 3.0 Preview

reasons: The four-run join on SQS message ID is solid work. Fresh pods, an empty queue, separate order ranges, the preview flag confirmed inside each pod and a jar hash check make each count trustworthy.

The title and opening claim more than the evidence shows. Splunk was never checked for the receive-telemetry runs (the post says so itself), and the receive spans are not in the producer's trace. The preview's own span tree shows only process and delete under the producer context, and there are 72 receive spans for 100 messages.

The repo path in Step 1 and the footer (showmerit/labs/otel-java-agent-3-0-preview-sqs-receive-spans-one-trace) does not match the lab's LAB_URL (Abhimanyu9988.github.io/labs/opentelemetry-java-agent-3-0-preview-on). A reader who copies the commands would hit a path that does not exist.
The evidence report marks splunk_preview_traces_found as self_reported, not corroborated, and its headline check failed ('3.0 Preview' not found in evidence).

Clear reader, and the four-row table is a real finding. With receive telemetry on, the shared-trace count goes from 0 of 100 to 100 of 100. The Splunk operation-name table is useful and goes beyond the docs.

Issue 19414, which the post cites, already says that under stable semconv the SQS process span's parent is the ambient context whatever the receive flag is set to. The post should present its result as the measured confirmation of what maintainers described, not as a discovery.
The span-tree code blocks use hand-written <queue> and <producer context> placeholders, so they don't read like real agent output. A trimmed excerpt from 05-fix.log would be more convincing.
The checklist and the 'What I didn't test' section deal with trade-offs honestly, and the tone credits OpenTelemetry and Splunk throughout.

Demand is weak, as the brief says. The only signal is issue 19433 (open, 6 comments) and the OpenTelemetry blog asking users to try the preview. There is no search volume and there are no reactions, so 3 is the ceiling.
Timing is good: the 3.0 preview is current, and the blog shows no SQS example.

'Receive Spans Now Stay in One Trace' is not how users describe this, and it is not what was measured. A headline built around renamed operations, or around SQS consumers staying in the producer's trace, matches the reader's decision better.

brief.reader: Platform engineer running Spring Boot services that exchange messages over Amazon SQS, with the OTel Java agent and Splunk Observability Cloud
brief.decision: Whether their SQS traces, and the span and operation names their Splunk APM filters and charts use, change under the Java agent's 3.0 messaging defaults, which they can preview today
brief.question: Will OTel Java agent 3.0 still put an SQS producer and its consumer in one trace in Splunk, and what changes in the spans?
brief.takeaway: One environment variable on the agent you already run shows 3.0's messaging behaviour on a real SQS queue today: whether each message stays in one trace, whether consumers link back to the producer, with and without receive telemetry, and which operation names Splunk APM then holds, so filters and charts can be checked before 3.0 is the default.
brief.adds: The OpenTelemetry blog shows 3.0's messaging changes with Kafka and Pulsar examples and describes no SQS result. This post runs the same two Spring Boot services on a real SQS queue in four configurations, counts per message the shared traces, links and span names, and reads sampled traces back from Splunk APM.
brief.open_question: With OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_COMMON_V3_PREVIEW=true on agent 2.33.1, how many of 400 SQS messages keep their producer and process spans in one trace, how many process spans link to the producer, what are the spans named, and how do those counts change with receive telemetry on, compared with the default agent on the same queue?
tradeoffs: The 2.33.1 preview can still change before 3.0, as the OpenTelemetry blog says
The preview flag also changes database and code conventions; this run measures messaging spans only
Single-message @SqsListener only; batch listeners follow a different model
The four runs are sequential on the same services and queue, not side by side; span structure is measured, not timing
Preview runs report under their own deployment.environment so Splunk keeps the two modes apart
